hints: Compare person J and person K side by side and count the large, dark-staining cells with nuclei. Which smear has many more of them?

Remember red blood cells have no nucleus and are small and pale, while white blood cells like lymphocytes are larger with a dark nucleus. Decide which cell type is increased in K, then read across that row of the table.
walkthrough:
**Compare the two smears carefully**

Person J is our healthy control. Their smear is almost all small, pale red blood cells with very few dark cells.

Person K has the same background of red blood cells, but has many extra large, dark-staining nucleated cells scattered all over.

**Identify which cell type has changed**

The small pale cells without nuclei are red blood cells. Their number looks similar in J and K.

The large dark cells are white blood cells, lymphocytes. Person K clearly shows an increase in lymphocytes, not a decrease.

**Use the table to match increase to disorder**

Look at the lymphocyte row of the table:
$$ \text{lymphocyte increase = chronic leukaemia, decrease = sepsis} $$
Since person K shows a lymphocyte increase, the disorder must be chronic leukaemia.

options.A: This causes a decrease in neutrophils, but person K shows an increase in dark white blood cells, not a decrease.
options.B: This causes an increase in red blood cells, but the red blood cell background looks similar in J and K.
options.C: This causes a decrease in lymphocytes, which is the opposite of what we see. Person K has many more lymphocytes than J.
options.D: Correct. Person K has many extra lymphocytes compared to healthy person J, and the table shows lymphocyte increase matches chronic leukaemia.
